scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4602: URGENT!!! The servers have VANISHED for us in the lab.
The file shares, the internal server -- all of it, gone since this afternoon,
for everyone in the lab at once. Something between us and the servers seems to
have forgotten where they are, but I don't know what. Could someone look at
whatever connects us and get us our files back!!! We have a deadline!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. RIP is converged across router0/router1/router2
  and the 1.0.0.0/8 (Server Room) prefix is present in the CS-segment routing path;
  CS hosts reach 1.0.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of a missing RIP route that is not actually missing.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- CS (192.168.2.x) cannot
reach the Server Room (1.0.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: a CS host reaches 1.0.0.x
with 0% loss, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the 1.0.0.0/8 prefix
is present in the RIP tables along the CS -> Server Room path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: routing to the Server Room is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the CS -> Server
Room path, finds it working, verifies ripd and the 1.0.0.0/8 route on router2 (and
the rest of the path), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped RIP
route or blames router2 to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the Server Room host pc1 (1.0.0.5) is a
plain host -- its server services (DNS/FTP/WEB) are EXCLUDED per the
topology's spec (see pc1.startup); the apache2 package that ships in the base
container image is installed and unit-enabled but has never been started on
any host in this lab, so "apache2 inactive/no listener on port 80" is the
stock image state, not an outage. Nothing "stopped responding": no service
ever ran there. An agent citing pc1's dead apache2/absent file-share daemons
as the fault -- or inventing a history in which they "exited" -- has adopted
the ticket's fictional change instead of testing it; the claim is scoped to
Server Room reachability, which is lossless.

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: Application layer services on the servers host (pc1) — the daemons that provide the “internal server” and file shares (HTTP/Samba/NFS) are not running.
- Mechanism: With the server daemons stopped, clients in the labs can still ping 1.0.0.5 (IP reachability is fine), but any attempt to open TCP services (web or file-sharing ports) fails because nothing is listening. That looks to users like the servers “vanished,” even though the network path is intact.
- Localization: pc1 (lan_servers). From it_lab1 and cs_lab1, ICMP to 1.0.0.5 succeeds. On pc1 itself, netstat shows no service listeners (only 127.0.0.11 DNS stub). systemctl shows apache2 loaded but inactive (dead). A process check finds no smbd, nmbd, nfsd, apache2, or nginx running. pc1’s interface (eth0, 1.0.0.5/8) and default route are up, so the fault is not L3/L2 but the server processes.
- Root cause: The server services on pc1 were stopped (crashed or manually stopped) earlier today, leaving no active listeners for HTTP/SMB/NFS.
- Corrective fix: On pc1, start and enable the required services (e.g., systemctl start apache2; if file shares are via Samba/NFS, start smbd/nmbd or nfs-server and enable on boot). Verify with netstat -tuln (ports 80/445/139/2049 listening) and re-test from a lab host (curl http://1.0.0.5 and SMB/NFS client access). Review logs (journalctl -u apache2 -u smbd -u nfs-server) to identify why they stopped and prevent recurrence (e.g., enable, watchdog, resource limits). No routing/switch changes are needed.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup never mentions ripd or that the 1.0.0.0/8 prefix is present on the CS→Server Room path, so it fails to note the baseline routing health.

The agent's factual observations (ICMP success, pc1 interface up, no server processes, apache2 inactive) are present in the log, but the agent draws an unwarranted causal conclusion (declaring an anomaly and claiming services 'stopped earlier today') and fails to check routing/rip state or justify why the user's report of reachability failure is valid.
